_comment: THE REPOSITORY ROOT's DECLARATION — what this instance IS and which directories it holds. SPLIT back out of `folio-assistant.config.json` on 2026-09-21, when the owner reversed `b5f0` §1's REPLACE ruling and took its other option: `<name>.json` for the declaration, `<name>.config.json` for the config, so the pair is legible from the filenames alone. Before the split both files ended `.config.json` and were told apart only by which directory they sat in and whether they carried a `name` — two schemas, two readers, one filename shape, which is the confusion `b5f0` §1 named when it recorded the option. Read by `readDeclaration` against `CatHarnessDeclarationSchema`; its sibling `folio-assistant.config.json` is read by `readHarnessConfig` and carries `contentType`. The root is the one instance where these were merged, because its instance directory IS the repository root — every other instance already had them in different directories.

_title_comment: The HUMAN display name, for the LHS navbar's harness tabs. Owner, 2026-09-21: "harnesses should list the names (they should be named in schmeas, e.g. cat-boostrap should be named 'Boostrap', f-a => Folio Assistant, cat-harness => C@T Harness)". `name` stays the machine identifier that filenames, `needs` edges and `declaredBy` resolve against; `title` is what a reader sees and nothing resolves against. Bean t3n8.
title: Folio Assistant
description: The repository itself, acting as an initialized instance. NAMED `folio-assistant-checkout` rather than `folio-assistant`, which `cat-harness/harness.json` already uses: two declarations sharing a name makes `declaredBy` and a sticky's `contributedBy` ambiguous, so a directory can be attributed to the wrong instance while reading correctly. It declares the directories a person drops things into, which belong to the checkout rather than to any one layer inside it.

directories.description: The incoming queue of the document-ingestion pipeline for THIS checkout — raw files as dropped, before ingestion. Distinct from `cat-harness/uploads/`, which is the harness layer's own queue: the two are different instances' directories that happen to share an id, not one directory declared twice. NOT L1 and NOT greppable as corpus; a source sitting here reads as absent to every consumer while the file is on disk.

_assets_comment: THE REPOSITORY'S OWN TWO FILES, declared here as of 2026-09-20 (issue #592). Before that the root instance declared NO assets at all, and `cat-harness` declared both of these with `scope: "repository"` — so the file an agent reads first was simultaneously "what this repository is" and "what the cat-harness layer is", and no instance owned it. `check:subgraph-coverage` reported nothing, because the asset DID resolve; it resolved to the wrong file's job, which is a distinction that check could not make until this split gave it two files to tell apart. The owner settled the fork on 2026-09-20: split them, so every instance owns exactly one README and one AGENTS.md, the root's being the INDEX over the others.

assets.title: AGENTS.md — folio-assistant
assets.description: The file every cold agent reads first, and the rules that bind in EVERY layer of this checkout. A layer's own AGENTS.md augments it and never restates it. `source` names the bootstrap instance it descends from, so "is this still what it was copied from" is a question that can be ASKED — 'it was copied at init' is not an answer. This provenance sits here rather than on cat-harness's because THIS is the file bootstrap copies at initialisation; cat-harness's own is authored in place and carries no source.

assets.title: folio-assistant
assets.description: The repository's reader-facing entry point, and the INDEX over every instance in it: its `cat-harness:instances` section is generated from the declarations themselves, giving each instance both an agent entry (AGENTS.md, memories) and a human one (README, docs). Generated sections are written by `readme:sync` only where the file already carries their markers, and `readme:audit` verifies every other link.

_needs_comment: The layer this instance sits on. Owner, 2026-09-20: "So bootsteap, cat harness, fa-core, f-a, from bottom to top." Declared rather than hardcoded in the navbar, so the ordering is a fact of the repository and not of whichever consumer needed it first.
